chapter: WWL and the Roosevelt Fountain Lounge
title: The Fountain Lounge band at the Roosevelt Hotel
summary: The interviewer and Frank recall Seymour Weiss keeping musicians working, and where the Fountain Lounge sat in the Roosevelt.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: An hour and a half a day. Who was the bass player you replaced? Louis Macenthal. Louis Macenthal. And you want to know the funny thing about that job? Because I started with...
You started with... You played with us a while.

Well, I was with them when they started because we came right out of the blue room. So Seymour wanted to keep Albert working, keep a couple of us working. And it was Sandy, Sandy and Albert and... Gordon. Gordon and Louis Macenthal and myself and Sal Franzel and Benny Legas.

And Seymour told us, he says, he's not paying a lot of money, but he says, you've got a job. He says, and you don't do anything between 1230 and 1230 and 1230. You don't do anything except eat lunch so you can play music.
So where was this place? That is the Fountain Lounge in the Roosevelt Hotel.
And we stayed in... You say downstairs from where the station was? The station was upstairs in the Roosevelt?
The station was upstairs in the Roosevelt on the second floor. And we played downstairs. Today, well, they didn't... The Fountain Lounge disappeared now. No, the Fountain Lounge is a Sazerac...
No, it's a Sazerac one. The Sazerac one? Yeah. And the coffee shop is now Bailey's.
